title: Third-Party Model Evaluation Access Term Sheet (draft)
content:
Purpose
This term sheet captures baseline commercial and security controls for short-term, limited-access model evaluation environments provided to third parties ("Vendor Evaluations"). It is intended to be attached as an exhibit to vendor engagement letters or non-production evaluation DPAs.

Scope and intended use
- Applies to time-boxed evaluation access where a third party (vendor, partner, or customer prospective partner) requests live access to a model or evaluation sandbox for the purposes of verification, benchmarking, or feature testing.
- Not intended for production integration, fine-tuning, or model weight transfer. Any request for persistent model artifacts or training data triggers a separate legal & sec review.

Key definitions (short form)
- "Evaluation Environment": an isolated, ephemeral tenant (sandbox) in Redwood infrastructure provisioned for Vendor Evaluation.
- "Evaluation Data": queries, prompts, datasets, or telemetry submitted by the third party during the evaluation period.
- "Ephemeral Token": short-lived credential scoped to an Evaluation Environment and set of API calls.
- "Evidence Package": logs, audit exports, and forensic snapshots produced on termination for compliance requests.

Access model and authentication
- Access granted via Ephemeral Tokens (default TTL: 24 hours). Long-lived tokens require explicit sec approval and a business justification.
- Tokens are scoped by route (e.g., /generate, /embed) and rate-limited by default to low-throughput profiling quotas.
- MFA strongly recommended for named user accounts and required for any privileged console access.
- Identity providers: OIDC-only for enterprise customers; vendors use pre-approved vendor accounts with RBAC.

Environment isolation and allowed operations
- Evaluation Environments are logically isolated (network namespaces, separate KV caches, isolated model runtime instances).
- Allowed operations: generate (no model weight extraction), embeddings generation, structured-output evaluation, limited streaming.
- Disallowed: weight export, on-device runtime, persistent KV writes that survive environment teardown, and unbounded bulk inference on customer-owned datasets.
- Vendor is prohibited from aggregating outputs to reconstruct training data or model internals.

Data handling and minimization
- Redwood will not retain Evaluation Data beyond the agreed retention window (default 30 days) except for ephemeral logs required for troubleshooting.
- Customer/vendor may request shorter retention or immediate purge; purge requests are honored within 24 hours (operational SLA).
- Where Evaluation Data includes customer-owned PII, the vendor must mark such elements prior to submission using provided metadata tags; Redwood will apply additional redaction and pseudonymization heuristics before storage.
- Residual KV/prefix caches are scrubbed at environment teardown; forensic copies retained only where required by an active legal hold.

Observability, telemetry, and evidence
- Redwood will produce an Evidence Package on termination or upon customer request: API call logs (redacted), model variant used, start/end timestamps, retention actions taken.
- Evidence Package excludes full prompt text if configured by customer — alternative: provide redacted prompt + token-level trace.
- Audit exports are digitally signed and timestamped.

Security controls and allowed tooling
- Network egress: evaluation environments default to deny-all egress except to controlled metrics and logging endpoints. Special egress (for remote benchmarking) must be approved and routed via TLS + egress proxy.
- No SSH or remote shell access to runtime nodes for vendors.
- Allowed tooling: browser-based console (read-only for infra details), API with scoped keys, and limited SFTP for test-data upload to a pre-approved bucket (uploads are scanned for secrets).

Model stewardship and provenance
- Redwood will identify the exact model ID, commit hash, and runtime config used for each evaluation session in the Evidence Package.
- Vendors may not claim ownership of model weights or derivative rights based on evaluation activity. Any downstream use beyond evaluation requires a separate license.

Liability, indemnity, and limitations
- Redwood liability for breaches arising solely from Redwood's fault is capped at the fees paid by the requesting party for the evaluation period (standard cap).
- Exclude consequential damages and lost profits. For claims involving customer PII or regulated data, negotiated damages & remedies may apply and should be escalated to Legal.
- Vendor indemnifies Redwood for misuse of Evaluation Data that violates export controls, sanctions, or causes regulatory fines.

Incident response and notification
- Redwood will notify the requesting party within 48 hours of confirmed security incidents affecting the Evaluation Environment.
- For incidents involving regulated data exfiltration we follow the standard incident escalation runbook (linked artifact SEC-4321).

Termination, sequester, and evidence handback
- Standard termination of an Evaluation Environment occurs at the agreed end-date or earlier by either party with 24 hours' notice.
- On termination, Redwood performs automated purge tasks and generates an Evidence Package. Where required by contract, Redwood will perform a forensic snapshot and transfer the Evidence Package via secure transfer under an NDA.
- For legal holds, Redwood will preserve environment artifacts for the hold period; preservation actions are logged and included in the Evidence Package.

Operational SLAs (non-production)
- Provisioning SLA: 48–72 hours to provision a new Evaluation Environment (shorter for high-priority channel).
- Purge SLA: 24 hours to purge data on request.
- Evidence export SLA: 5 business days for signed Evidence Packages.

Commercial terms (term-sheet level)
- Fee model: one-time evaluation seat fee + metered usage (per-token/compute) during evaluation. Volume discounts apply for multiple parallel seats.
- Default trial period: 14 days. Extensions subject to negotiated fees.
- IP: evaluation activity does not transfer model IP. Vendor feedback may be used by Redwood for product development unless covered by a separate confidentiality assignment.

Open items / TODOs
- Decide default retention: 14 vs 30 days (sec/legal trade-off).
- Add explicit export controls clause and reference to sanctions screening.
- Template NDA language for Evidence Package transfer (legal to draft).
- Operationalize console-only “redacted prompts” mode for PII-heavy evaluations (ENG ticket: CON-PR-342).

References and cross-links
- See SEC-4321 for incident runbook.
- Confluence draft: vendor-eval-access-guidelines (linked).

Sign-off
- Security: ____________________ (name, date)
- Legal: ____________________ (name, date)
- Product (hosted API): ____________________ (name, date)
- Eng (serving runtime): ____________________ (name, date)

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working-term-sheet intended to be light-weight and attachable to evaluation engagements. Keep the technical controls narrow and operationally feasible.
- If we expect more than 3 concurrent external evaluations per customer, escalate to dedicated Dedicated/Private deployment sales motion.
- For any request involving model fine-tuning, model weights, or long-term storage, do not use this term sheet; open a formal DPA+SLA negotiation and security review.
